item.title: Chureito Pagoda: The Iconic Five-Storey Pagoda With Mount Fuji — Guide
item.description: Chureito Pagoda is a five-storey red pagoda set on a hillside above Fujiyoshida, reached by a climb of just under 400 steps, and frames one of Japan’s most iconic views: the vermilion pagoda in the foreground with Mount Fuji rising behind it across the town below. The scene is especially striking in spring when cherry blossoms surround the pagoda, and in autumn with coloured foliage, drawing photographers from around the world to what has become one of the most recognisable images of Japan.

item.title: Yoshida Fire Festival: Giant Torches Marking Fuji's Climbing Season Close — Guide
item.description: The Yoshida Fire Festival, held each late August in Fujiyoshida, is one of Japan’s three most unusual festivals, traditionally marking the close of Mount Fuji’s climbing season with a dramatic display of fire. On the main evening, dozens of giant torches, some three metres tall, are lit along the town’s main street alongside smaller fires outside homes and shops, filling the streets with flame and smoke as portable shrines are paraded through, in a centuries-old ritual tied to the Sengen shrine and Fuji worship, praying for safety on the mountain.

item.title: Yoshida Udon: Fujiyoshida's Famously Firm, Chewy Noodles — Guide
item.description: Yoshida udon, a specialty of Fujiyoshida at the foot of Mount Fuji, is renowned for having some of the firmest, chewiest udon noodles in all of Japan, a texture so distinctively robust that it has become the dish’s defining characteristic. Typically served in a broth blending miso and soy sauce, topped with boiled cabbage, sometimes horse meat, and a spicy condiment called suridane, the dish is often found at simple, family-run shops, some operating out of private homes with limited lunchtime hours, giving it a genuinely local, unpretentious character.
